note: Written by Claude from reputable outlets (Reuters via syndication partners, AP, ABC News, Bernama, Korea Herald, JoongAng Daily, The Standard, Business Standard and others); source under each story. Japan, South Korea, India and the US sections are shorter because fewer reputable reports could be retrieved this morning. Sports excluded.

items.headline: Oracle scraps $7bn chip-leasing deal with Tencent
items.summary: Oracle has cancelled a five-year lease that would have given Tencent access to roughly 100,000 advanced AI chips in Oracle's Southeast Asian data centres, the FT reported, after US officials raised concerns. Guangdong officials had reportedly also urged Tencent to back domestic chips. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

items.headline: Palantir revenue nearly doubles; full-year outlook raised
items.summary: Palantir's third-quarter revenue rose 96% to $2.31 billion, beating forecasts, and it lifted its full-year revenue guidance to about $8.53 billion. US commercial sales overtook US government sales for the first time.

items.headline: SpaceX picks Qualcomm for Starlink Mobile 5G network
items.summary: SpaceX selected Qualcomm's Dragonwing platforms for Starlink Mobile's 5G network. Qualcomm shares edged up while SpaceX's fell about 6%.

items.headline: Big Tech leads Dow surge after midterms
items.summary: Amazon and Microsoft each rose about 7% and Apple more than 6% on Wednesday, making them among the Dow's biggest gainers as markets reacted to the Democratic sweep. Apple had reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion earlier in the week.

items.headline: Amdocs plunges a third on weak outlook; Duolingo soars
items.summary: Amdocs shares sank about 36% after it gave a much weaker fiscal 2027 outlook, citing a legal dispute with T-Mobile. Duolingo jumped about 19% on stronger third-quarter results and a raised full-year forecast.

items.headline: Dow jumps 3% as Democrats sweep Congress
items.summary: The Dow closed up 1,569 points (3.0%) at 53,356, with the S&P 500 up 1.6% at 7,689 and the Nasdaq up 1.4%. Only four Dow stocks fell as investors welcomed reduced uncertainty after the midterms.

items.headline: Brent falls below $100 for the first time in weeks
items.summary: Brent crude dropped about $10 a barrel during Wednesday's US session to trade under $100, extending a slide driven by hopes for an end to the US-Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts.

items.headline: Gold climbs back above $4,000 as dollar weakens
items.summary: Gold futures rose nearly 3% to about $4,053 an ounce and silver gained almost 5% to $52, as the dollar sold off and investors initially sought safety after the election results.

items.headline: CVS to split into two companies
items.summary: CVS Health announced a plan to separate into two companies by the first half of 2028; its shares slipped about 2%.

items.headline: FIS sinks a quarter after CFO exit and outlook cut
items.summary: Fidelity National Information Services fell about 25% after it cut its full-year outlook, announced its CFO's departure and was downgraded by JPMorgan. Block, by contrast, rose about 16% after its results.

items.headline: Singapore to toughen haze law, with fines up to S$20m
items.summary: Environment Minister Grace Fu said the status quo is "no longer tenable" after the recent haze. Proposed changes would let the government appoint private assessors to investigate firms, raise maximum fines to S$1 million a day (capped at S$20 million) and bar companies from dealing with suspected contributors.

items.headline: MAS tells banks to review ties with haze-linked firms
items.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore has advised banks to impose conditions on, or cut ties with, companies that may have breached environmental laws. Singapore has also sent information requests to 10 Singapore-registered companies over possible haze links.

items.headline: Singapore to push haze pact as ASEAN chair next year
items.summary: Ms Fu said Singapore will work with member states to strengthen implementation of the regional transboundary haze agreement when it chairs ASEAN in 2027.

items.headline: Rena Lee becomes first Singaporean elected ICJ judge
items.summary: Ambassador for International Law Rena Lee was elected a judge of the International Court of Justice, the first Singaporean to hold the post.

items.headline: Haze drove rise in emergency and polyclinic visits
items.summary: Haze-related visits to emergency departments rose 20% and polyclinic visits 25% between early September and mid-October.

items.headline: Indonesian police say Prabowo was illegally wiretapped
items.summary: Police confirmed that President Prabowo Subianto, ministers, officials, politicians and journalists had been illegally wiretapped since 2025 by three senior officers.

items.headline: Indonesia's inflation within target; factory index at 54
items.summary: Indonesia's finance ministry said October inflation of 3.23% is within the government's target range, and the manufacturing index rose to 54.

items.headline: Thai PM orders defences against cyberattacks on food supply
items.summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told agencies to prepare for possible cyberattacks on food storage and supply systems.

items.headline: Philippine police pledge action on attacks against journalists
items.summary: The Philippine National Police promised stronger measures to hold attackers of journalists accountable, while local shares slipped on fears of higher October inflation.

items.headline: Vietnam and Laos vow to turn pledges into projects
items.summary: Vietnamese PM Le Minh Hung met Lao National Assembly President Sonexay Siphandone in Hanoi, while Laos sought closer oversight of planned expressway, rail and port links with Vietnam.

items.headline: Nikkei drops 3% as US midterms hit AI stocks
items.summary: Japanese shares fell sharply on worries that Democratic gains could bring tighter rules on data centres and slow AI spending. SoftBank Group lost about 7%, Kioxia 10% and Tokyo Electron 5% in early trade.

items.headline: Yen firms as dollar slides after vote
items.summary: The dollar weakened to about 157.6 yen as Democrats gained ground in the US elections.

items.headline: Kospi swings wildly before closing higher
items.summary: The Kospi opened up 2.4%, sank to 5,421 by midday, then recovered to close 0.6% higher at 5,684 as battery makers rallied; Samsung SDI jumped nearly 12%.

items.headline: Court upholds Yoon's election-disinformation conviction
items.summary: A Seoul appeals court upheld former president Yoon Suk Yeol's 18-month suspended sentence for spreading election disinformation, a ruling that could require his party to repay nearly $30 million.

items.headline: President Lee launches YouTube Q&A show
items.summary: Lee Jae Myung will debut "The President's Y", hosted by former MBC anchor Son Jung-eun, to explain policy decisions, with episodes every two to three weeks.

items.headline: Taylor says government 'in denial' after rate hike
items.summary: Opposition Leader Angus Taylor attacked the government's economic record after the RBA's fifth hike this year, proposing $31 billion in cuts to climate and housing programmes.

items.headline: Senate blocks private health rebate cut for over-65s
items.summary: The Coalition, Greens and crossbenchers blocked Labor's bill to wind back the private health insurance rebate for those 65 and over, which would have saved $3 billion over four years. Labor says more savings will come in December's mid-year update.

items.headline: Albanese rejects means-testing battery and EV schemes
items.summary: The PM dismissed business calls to means-test the home battery and electric vehicle schemes, saying the government would not cut health or school funding.

items.headline: Ai Group warns AI data-centre boom is crowding out the economy
items.summary: Ai Group chief Innes Willox said the AI build-out is pulling resources from other sectors; the May budget relied on data centres and renewables for almost all forecast business investment growth.

items.headline: Commonwealth agrees on UK slavery apology
items.summary: Albanese welcomed consensus at CHOGM on a UK apology for slavery; UK PM Andy Burnham has left the door open, though reparations appear unlikely.

items.headline: Democrats take control of both houses of Congress
items.summary: Democrats won majorities in the House and Senate, including victories in long-time Republican strongholds, in a major rebuke of President Trump. Vice-President JD Vance blamed the losses on the Iran war.
items.source: AP via Euronews; The Standard; Yahoo News

items.headline: Talarico beats Paxton to win Texas Senate seat
items.summary: Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton, ending the GOP's 32-year statewide winning streak in Texas.

items.headline: Supreme Court rejects bid to set aside California ballots
items.summary: The court turned down the Trump administration's request to set aside 20,000 California ballots it had flagged as likely non-citizen votes.

items.headline: Early vote ran 10 million ahead of 2022
items.summary: About 10 million more people voted early than at the same point in the 2022 midterms, AP reported; Gallup found 47% of voters called the Iran war extremely important to their vote.
items.source: AP and Gallup via Yahoo News

items.headline: Beijing confirms talks on first US-Russia-China summit
items.summary: China said it is "in communication with relevant parties" about a meeting of the three heads of state, reportedly on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen. It called the US midterms a domestic affair.

items.headline: Banks seek 200bn yuan to fund share buybacks
items.summary: Chinese banks applied for more than 200 billion yuan in loan quotas this week to finance listed companies' share purchases, the central bank said, as Beijing props up the stock market.

items.headline: Wang Yi hosts Saudi and Iranian security chiefs
items.summary: China urged against a return to conflict in the Gulf, backed US-Iran negotiations and said it would help seek a settlement on reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

items.headline: China rejects UK report linking it to AI-enabled hacking
items.summary: The foreign ministry called the accusation baseless and said Britain was using it to curb China's AI development.

items.headline: Investor says Chinese AI models nearly match US
items.summary: Qiming Venture Partners' Duane Kuang said Chinese model capabilities are now very close to America's, attributing the valuation gap to revenue and profitability differences.

items.headline: Sensex rises for a fifth straight session
items.summary: The Sensex gained 384 points to 77,301 and the Nifty closed at 23,961, led by media, realty and metal stocks as oil eased; IT was the only sector to fall, with TCS down 2.5%.

items.headline: Cabinet approves ₹2,814 crore critical-minerals scheme
items.summary: The scheme offers a 30% capital subsidy over five years for two lithium and two nickel processing plants, to cut reliance on imported refined minerals.
